This game is awesome. All of the fun of the old mobile game with a new isometric top-down view? Sign me up. However, as a PC game, it should be held to much higher standards than its older versions. The infinitely generating map is great, and I love the loot box system, but I feel like there's too many of them that it takes away from the thrill of finding one. It would be a lot cooler if they were more rare and as a compromise, their loot tables could be more skewed towards higher leveled/more powerful weapons? I would also love to see more maps, like in Zombieville 2. You had the mall, the suburbs, the city, but this game only has the suburbs. A city map, a mall map, maybe even more maps like a nature/campground map or a gated community map? And speaking of level design, I love the progression of the zombie strength and variety increasing as time goes on, but you barely notice it happening. If the UI did a better job at letting you know that you've went up a scale in difficulty (maybe like a full screen alert), then the progression could feel a lot more noticeable, and getting to higher difficulties and staying alive longer could feel much more impactful and immersive. I have noticed a bug in my playthrough (although it could be a feature) where the zombies are unable to get to you if you move behind a fence or a lamp post. They sort of just get stuck and run in place until you walk around them to a place they can get to through a straight line. It would also be really fun to have a small chance of getting ammo from breaking bins and mail posts, and also being able to drive cars through the map as well. Also, a more fleshed out multiplayer experience would be incredible. It's always hard to get together with a group of friends to play a co-op game since so many people have so many different schedules. An auto-fill random search multiplayer mode would make this game tons better! I love this game so much, I've played Zombieville 2 for practically my entire life on my phone and everyone I've shared it with has instantly fallen in love with it and wanted to keep playing it. Hearing about it coming out on PC as a sequel was the most shocking and exciting news I've heard in a while, and I'm so happy to finally be able to play it! I'm excited to continue playing it, and I hope that it continues to receive the love, attention and devotion that it deserves.

Like other reviewers have said. Starting with positives: The game plays really well, The art is great and works, guns feel good. I like the different characters, haven't even tried multiplayer yet but assuming it will be fun with a friend. Cons: overpriced for what it is currently. Would feel totally justified in the purchase if it was around 5 bucks, but at 10 it's steep for a "high score" arcade style bullet hell shooter with meta progression that is there to essentially pad time played. I'm addicted! But not for long. Just a sucker for getting all the "upgrades", like other reviews have stated, this are mainly just stat buffs to kind of artificially inflate playtime. I can honesty see myself quitting and never picking it back up once I unlock everything and get all the upgrades. It doesn't have that "one more run" vibe without the meta progression, this is its biggest flaw. As pointed out by others, would love to see different characters have unique character passives/perks, A mode that is rougelite would be really cool with a friend, between levels you strategize on upgrades and starting weapons and such. I think the game would work better if it was level based like similar games such as "Brotato", You get weapons and upgrades in a level and after levels, they carry over to the next level which is more of a challenge, your build slowly starts to form, and you made good decisions with good RNG or you fall behind and get overrun. The game would benefit from something like that greatly. I think loose rougelike elements and kind of converting the gameplay to rougelite would make the game much more enjoyable. TLDR suggestion: rougelike elements with meta progression in character progress, make a "build" for a character with various perks and upgrades (as well as unique character passive to each character model). Then rougelite style gameplay loop once you hop in a game solo or with a friend, in levels collect guns, upgrade characters/guns between levels by getting various "offered" upgrades (these wouldn't be purchasable, maybe an intense sprint skill on a cooldown that tackles zombies when you move through them damaging/killing them, maybe a revive for yourself or a teamate etc stuff like that.... Then! with the money you collect in a level upgrade stuff further while progressing, think more stat type stuff outside of game modifying perk type choices at the end of a level. This would add so much more replayability. Game suffers from feeling to samey every run, need some sort of "builds" to focus on and try to pull off IMO. edit: so after getting all the upgrades (working on last few) it's worse than I thought. Late-game consists of picking the mageblade and standing in a corner holding the attack button if you actually want to collect enough money in your lifetime to get all the gun upgrades... which are pointless anway though because every gun other than the mageblade sucks at level 40+, I am quite literally laying my phone on the mouse after getting in a corner, and periodically checking back to collect the money on the ground. I doubt it will be turned into a more traditional bullet hell rougelite but it has great potential, it's systems are good but not cohesive enough to be a good game, and the balance is wack.

Feels like I'm back playing an Xbox 360 Live Arcade game. There is a lot of charm and love to this game. It's also very addicting! I will say I haven't tried coop yet. My biggest QOL change that I have seen others also bring up is customizing the keybindings. Its a bit incontinent but it still find it enjoyable to play. There is only one map as of now, and 5 zombie types. It does have a lot of weapons and upgrades though. For $10, I would certainly say I got my moneys worth. I still would like to see more added to this game for more variety. I might buy $5 worth of DLC not for just a new map but extra everything. Considering it might be a solo dev again, I'm not sure where this game might go and what amount of work it requires to do so. I really like this game and hope it grows in a sincere direction.

I wanted to like this, but holy canoli... this game wants you to play it one specific way and if you don't want to, you can go pound sand. The first two save games were completely wasted trying to enjoy my playthrough by using a melee build, then an explosives/elemental build. Nope. The game doesn't like that. I thought progression was monumentally slow, but then I randomly bought some weapons with two other types (shotgun/pistol/automatic) and respec'd to increase damage in those types. The melee range is way too short to be viable. Even with the perks to boost them, the first three weapon types I was drawn to are completely pointless. What a disappointment. EDIT: After a brief period of "playing it right" by exploiting the game's mechanics, I reached 100% achievements with a new save in fairly short order, and I can honestly say that this game is really annoying. Locating the 40 purple coins was agony. The irony of my first review is that the best late-game weapons are melee/elemental, but it takes so long to get them that you really shouldn't focus on those weapon types until the end... even though low level versions of those types are available AND necessary for using to unlock the more powerful versions.

I would absolutely give this a positive review if it seemed as though the devs were going to do more with it, but that doesn't seem to be the case. The game has 1 to 2 hours of interesting gameplay (if that), and then you've basically seen it all. Not really worth the $10 price in my opinion. If it were free, this review would be positive. There is only one map you can play on, different characters (which are solely cosmetic and have no difference on gameplay), zero bosses (just increasingly difficult waves), and a very large selection of guns that are kind of redundant and made obsolete by how overpowered melee weapons are (no ammo, infinite durability, fire knife is WAY TOO OP) These things are not really "bad" issues on their own. This game just suffers from a lack of content and optimization that could be fixed with a little attention, but there aren't currently any signs of it getting any, which makes the lack of content and balance issues seem a lot worse, especially with the price. Hopefully I'm wrong and the devs come back and do something cool with it. It's been less than a year since release, and I know it's a small team that is more used to making mobile games, but there really is a goldmine of potential here with the concept and mechanics. Plus, I really love the artstyle.

This is a recommend from me, but with caveats. The dev worked on this for years and clearly put a lot of love into it, so that makes it all the stranger that they released it, put out a handful of updates, then disappeared and haven't commented on this game since. I do NOT believe the game should be live-service, but the game is pretty bare-bones and it was suggested numerous times throughout development AND for a brief period afterward that there would likely be content updates released following the 1.0. As it is, it's a fun little game that's probably worth the price of admission, but the single map gets extremely repetitive extremely quickly, and neither the incremental weapon upgrades you unlock nor the funny character designs (while endearing and genuinely gorgeously stylized) are enough to keep me playing. I really wish the dev would've at least let people know they were no longer planning future updates or content, but the game is good fun as-is for about 10-15 hours, which is really all you can ask for from a $10 game.

The game is decent enough to play for the few hours it takes for 100% completion, but the dev should not even be allowed to keep it up for sale after abandoning it with such awful performance issues putting lots of unnecessary wear on players' hardware. This game showed lots of promise with six updates in less than a month after release, but there have been none since then so it can now be considered abandoned nostalgia bait. It is terribly unoptimized as it is averaging 85 FPS on max settings with a 5080 OC, which is less FPS than I get on Cyberpunk 2077 at max settings. GPU usage increases to 100% when in the upgrades area so clearly something has gone horribly wrong for top-end PCs to struggle with these mobile-quality graphics. Even though the Deck is powerful enough to run this at max rendering quality, it quickly overheats on any setting higher than the absolute minimum. A full charge lasts less than two hours when it should last at least four hours for a game like this. The developer continues to be active elsewhere on other projects but refuses to address any questions or issues regarding this game. There is no reason to buy this in its current state unless it is at least half off. Even then, there are plenty of much better games for the same price. Gameplay is accurate to how the originals would be if they were 3D. There is only one map and it gets boring quickly, as does the entire game since there are few enemy types and runs are repetitive with upgrades being the only difference. The shop needs a minimap or indicator upgrade to point to the nearest purple coin. Regarding the purple coins, only half of them can even be used and collecting all of them is only useful for the achievement and unlocking one of the best weapons in the game. There is no setting to change or even view controls which is a basic expectation for modern gaming. Some of the controls are awful and Steam Input is limited in how much it can compensate for this mistake. At high levels, there is money all over the ground so weapons on the ground can be difficult to see. With the right weapons and perks, players can survive indefinitely. It would be a pretty great game if not for the performance issues and lack of content.

Whoever labeled this game a roguelike/ roguelite clearly does not enjoy roguelikes or has no idea what a roguelike is. There are no real builds here just the same mobile game loop. However the core gameplay is solid fun is small dozes. How i wish the developers came back to this game and dropped the roguelike / lite tag and turned his into a fully packed game with multiple stages, a massive arsenal of weapons, powerups and zombies etc. Then this would be one of my favourite games of all time. Unfortunately as it is right now, its a demo of what could have been. A demo of a game with a price tag.
